reason: Eligibility and documentation agents find therapy furnished by the SNF reasonable, necessary and documented given the documented functional decline.
A 12-day hospital stay is asserted by both parties and the record shows ongoing skilled need (repeated medication adjustments), so the stay is treated as qualifying and SNF care as covered.
The appellant contests only liability, not coverage; nothing shows an admission order or support for inpatient level of care, so coverage is not supported.
The facts concern only briefing deadlines and show no qualifying stay or services, so coverage is not supported.
SNF admission followed a qualifying stay, and PT plateaued by Feb 7; the appellant argues only liability for non-covered services, implying early care covered and later care not.
Homebound status, skilled need and non-duplication with facility-required services are not established, so coverage is not supported.
Disputed dates follow therapy discharge, no qualifying stay length or ongoing skilled need is shown, so coverage is not supported.
Nurses relayed fluctuating glucose logs, insulin was repeatedly adjusted, and the skilled need was documented in visit notes.
The Feb 12-17 stay meets the 3-day requirement, SNF admission was direct for a condition treated in hospital, and skilled nursing need was documented.
Qualifying stay and direct admission support coverage initially, but therapy was discharged Sept 30 and later skilled need is not shown, so only the earlier period is covered.
Skilled need and an active written plan are only asserted by the appellant, and the beneficiary met goals by Sept 11, so coverage is not supported.
Skilled need and homebound status are only asserted, and aide-training or maintenance visits are not billable, so coverage is not supported.
Documented complications (UTIs, urosepsis, abscesses, fistula near colostomy) go beyond routine care and required skilled nursing.
Coverage is limited to part-time hours (28, up to 35 case by case), so only hours within that limit could be covered, not any excess.
Placement in a noncertified bed bars payment under the appropriate-bed rule despite the qualifying stay.
No patient-level clinical facts show the IRF requirements were met, so coverage is not supported.
SNF admission followed a qualifying psychiatric stay, and skilled observation of psychiatric symptoms and pneumonia was necessary and documented.
IRF admission after knee replacement with substantial functional deficits and IV/IM pain management supports medical necessity.
